hypotheses.statement: The text is rendered but has insufficient ink contrast against its background (e.g., near-white text on white or low-opacity filter applied).
hypotheses.prediction: Both versions will show the text element with style.color and style.backgroundColor having low luminance contrast (e.g., ΔL < 0.5) or an ancestor applying a filter reducing opacity.
hypotheses.falsifier: At least one version shows high luminance contrast (ΔL ≥ 0.5) between text color and background, with no opacity-reducing filters in ancestors.

hypotheses.statement: The text is rendered but fully covered by one or more opaque overlays stacked above it.
hypotheses.prediction: Both versions will have at least one element covering the text rect with backgroundColor not fully transparent and opacity ≥ 0.5.
hypotheses.falsifier: No element covers the text rect in either version, or all covering elements have fully transparent backgrounds or opacity < 0.5.

hypotheses.statement: The text is rendered but outside the viewport due to incorrect layout (e.g., negative margin, transform, or overflow) in transfer-a.
hypotheses.prediction: transfer-a will show the text element with rect.x < 0 or rect.y < 0 or rect.x + rect.width > viewport width or rect.y + rect.height > viewport height.
hypotheses.falsifier: The text element rect is fully within viewport bounds in transfer-a.

probe.question: What are the rendered pixels, covering elements, and computed styles for every match of the affected text in both versions?
probe.falsifier: Any version fails to provide the required measurements for all matches.
controls: Use the same viewport for both versions to ensure comparability.
Measure every match of the affected text, not just the first.
Sample points inside each text rect to detect all covering elements, not only the topmost.
Capture rendered pixels for the text rect and a reference background area.
Record computed styles and ancestor filters for each match.
limitations: Does not account for dynamic content changes after initial render.
Assumes the text element is uniquely identifiable by its content; if multiple matches exist, all are measured.
Reference background clip may not perfectly match the text's background in all cases.
